text: Android Honeycomb is the codename for the third major version of Android, developed for devices with larger screens, especially tablets, although it has been unofficially adapted for the Nexus One. It represents the eighth version of the Android operating system and is no longer supported as of November 14, 2016. Honeycomb was first released with the Motorola Xoom in February 2011. In addition to new features, it introduced a "holographic" user interface theme and an interaction model that expanded upon core Android functionalities such as multitasking, notifications, and widgets.
